AHF launches a $10 million allocation under the joint $22 million CERF–AHF Anticipatory Action framework for drought in 2026 (CERF: $12M; AHF: $10M).  The allocation aims to:  •	Mitigate drought impacts before crisis thresholds are reached through trigger-based early financing.  •	Protect lives, livelihoods and dignity in the most climate-exposed, severity 4+ districts.  •	Deliver integrated, household-level support, centered on multipurpose cash and early warning, complemented by agriculture, WASH, nutrition, health and protection measures.  •	Enhance speed, predictability and coherence of pooled fund responses under a unified AA framework aligned with the 2026 HNRP.  Lessons applied from 2025: simplified trigger activation, tighter geographic targeting, and streamlined response packages—making anticipatory action (AA) more operational, scalable and fit-for-purpose in Afghanistan’s climate-risk context.

The escalation of the Afghanistan-Pakistan conflict has compounded an already critical humanitarian situation in Afghanistan, particularly in border and displacement-affected areas where insecurity, population movements, and access constraints intersect with widespread explosive ordnance contamination. In this context, the AHF is launching a US$ 1.5 million Reserve Allocation to reduce the immediate humanitarian impact of explosive ordnance on conflict-affected and displacement-affected populations through targeted mine action interventions in high-risk and underserved locations.  The allocation aims to:  •	Reduce death, injury, and psychological harm among civilians, especially children, through targeted EO risk education and community-based risk communication in high-risk areas.  •	Improve safe access to humanitarian assistance, essential services, and population movement routes through explosive ordnance survey, spot tasks, quick response, and priority clearance.  •	Restore safer access to critical civilian infrastructure and livelihood assets, including schools, health facilities, housing/public spaces, agricultural land, grazing areas, and water/irrigation access points.  •	Improved local readiness to respond to newly emerging contamination threats by empowering and funding priority to local/national NGOs.    The allocation will be delivered through multiple partners, with a strong emphasis on empowering local NGOs and reinforcing localized response capacity. 2 national NGOs and 1 international NGOs are pre-identified for this allocation for an expedited allocation process.

This Reserve Allocation supports timely, pre-agreed anticipatory actions triggered by forecasts under the Fiji Anticipatory Action Framework (2025–2027). It prioritizes NGO-led, community-level early actions, including early warning, cash, and WASH/NFI support, complementing CERF and other risk financing mechanisms, with flexibility to pivot to other shocks or early response as needed.

This Reserve Allocation enables the timely delivery of pre agreed, life saving early actions ahead of tropical cyclone impacts in Vanuatu, ensuring partners can act within the narrow window between reliable forecast and landfall. The allocation strengthens localization by prioritizing NGO implemented, community level anticipatory actions that complement nationally coordinated and UN-led interventions under the Vanuatu Anticipatory Action Framework for Tropical Cyclones.     Building on a series of national engagement – including the first national Anticipatory Action consultation convened by the National Disaster Management Office (NDMO) and OCHA on 10 December 2025—the allocation scales last mile delivery of early actions aligned with the framework’s pre agreed triggers, agreed geographic prioritization, and national coordination arrangements.     The allocation aims to strengthen operational reach across Vanuatu’s multi island geography, where remoteness and logistics constraints often delay response after impact. The allocation forms part of a layered anticipatory financing architecture for Vanuatu, complementing CERF pre arranged funding and planned contributions from bilateral donors and regional instruments. This integrated approach enables more predictable, coordinated, and cost effective humanitarian action ahead of severe cyclone impacts.

The Regional Humanitarian Pooled Fund for Asia and the Pacific (RHPF-AP) – Bangladesh envelope seeks US$150 million to support life-saving humanitarian assistance under the 2025–2026 Joint Response Plan (JRP) for the Rohingya Humanitarian Crisis and address emerging needs from natural disasters.    Bangladesh hosts over one million Rohingya refugees alongside vulnerable host communities in Cox’s Bazar, one of the country’s poorest and most disaster-prone districts. Continued displacement from Myanmar, including 130,000 new arrivals in 2025 and 35,000 expected in 2026, has intensified humanitarian needs. The 2026 JRP targets 1.56 million people, with financial requirements of US$698.4 million, including US$495.3 million in Priority 1 life-saving interventions. Funding shortfalls have heightened food insecurity, malnutrition, protection risks, and exposure to climate-related hazards.    Bangladesh also faces recurrent climate shocks—cyclones, floods, landslides, and disease outbreaks—affecting millions annually. Between 2015 and 2024, disasters affected an average of 9.7 million people per year. In 2024 alone, Cyclone Remal and widespread flooding affected 18 million people, compounding vulnerabilities in refugee-hosting areas.    Managed by OCHA’s Regional Office for Asia and the Pacific (ROAP) under the Resident Coordinator (RC), the RHPF-AP Bangladesh envelope provides flexible, timely financing to priority sectors identified through coordinated humanitarian processes. Allocations are determined through a transparent, consultative mechanism involving an Advisory Board of local and international NGOs, UN agencies, cluster coordinators, donors, and government counterparts. Contributions are unearmarked and allocated based on agreed priorities.    The Fund operates through two windows: (i) Standard Allocations aligned with JRP priorities, and (ii) Reserve Allocations for rapid response to unforeseen emergencies. In 2026, the Fund will focus on acute food insecurity, malnutrition, inadequate WASH services, shelter and NFI gaps, health needs, protection risks including GBV and child protection, and preparedness for climate hazards. Key priorities include:    General food assistance and fresh food vouchers, with LPG support for safe cooking;    Prevention and treatment of acute malnutrition among children under five and pregnant and breastfeeding women;    Emergency WASH, health services, and support to field hospitals;    Emergency shelter and NFI assistance;    Protection services for individuals at heightened risk.    The RHPF-AP emphasizes localization, prioritizing national and local partners and promoting humanitarian action that is “as local as possible, as international as necessary.” Consolidated regional management ensures cost-efficiency and compliance with OCHA’s Global Guidelines for CBPFs.    Monitoring and accountability are central. A risk-based approach prioritizes high-risk projects, with field visits, third-party monitoring where required, and remote monitoring in access-constrained areas. Robust due diligence, financial oversight, reporting, audits, and UN oversight ensure transparency. The Fund upholds strong Accountability to Affected Populations (AAP) standards, including feedback mechanisms and strict compliance with the UN’s zero-tolerance policy on Sexual Exploitation and Abuse (SEA).    Through predictable, flexible, and principled pooled financing, the RHPF-AP Bangladesh envelope strengthens coordinated humanitarian leadership, addresses funding gaps, empowers local actors, and enables timely, life-saving assistance to the most vulnerable refugees and host communities.

Face à une détérioration soudaine de la situation sécuritaire et humanitaire dans la préfecture de la Vakaga, en particulier dans la zone frontalière avec le Soudan, le Coordonnateur Humanitaire lance une allocation de réserve (RA5) d’un montant de 3 mil-lions USD afin de permettre une réponse rapide, ciblée et intégrée aux besoins humanitaires les plus critiques.    Cette allocation est déclenchée par l’escalade des violences armées observée en septembre 2025  autour d’Am-Dafock, ayant entraîné des pertes civiles, la destruction de biens et le déplacement d’environ 5 000 personnes vers des zones déjà fragiles et faiblement couvertes par l’aide humanitaire. Dans un contexte de sous-financement chronique du HNRP et de contraintes d’accès accrues liées à l’insécurité et à l’isolement géographique de la Vakaga, cette allocation vise à prévenir une détériora-tion rapide des conditions de vie des populations affectées et à réduire les risques de protection, en particulier pour les femmes et les enfants.    À l’issue de consultations avec les clusters, les partenaires humanitaires et le Comité Consultatif du FH RCA, l’allocation sou-tiendra une réponse multisectorielle et contextualisée dans les secteurs de l’Eau, Hygiène et Assainissement (EHA), de la Santé, de la Protection et de la prévention et réponse aux Violences Basées sur le Genre (VBG). Les interventions cibleront à la fois les besoins vitaux immédiats des populations déplacées, hôtes et retournées, et la continuité de services essentiels dans des zones à très faible présence humanitaire, notamment à Am-Dafock, Ouanda-Djallé et Ouandja.    Conformément aux priorités stratégiques du Fonds, un minimum de 35 % des ressources sera alloué directement aux ONG na-tionales, y compris aux organisations locales de femmes, afin de renforcer la localisation et d’assurer une réponse plus rapide, pertinente et redevable dans un environnement opérationnel contraint.

Cette allocation s’inscrit dans la vision 2025 du Coordonnateur Humanitaire (CH) de la RCA et de la communauté humanitaire du pays, en combinant continuité opérationnelle, localisation, réponse rapide, approche sensible au genre et redevabilité. Elle vise également à renforcer les capacités des acteurs locaux, en particulier les organisations dirigées par des femmes (WLO), tout en maintenant la possibilité de répondre rapidement aux alertes humanitaires.            Les WLO, grâce à leur ancrage communautaire et leur présence dans les zones difficiles d’accès, jouent un rôle clé pour assurer la continuité de l’assistance et des réponses sensibles au genre. Cependant, leur accès limité aux financements directs (en raison de contraintes institutionnelles ou techniques) freine souvent leur potentiel.          Pour soutenir des réponses humanitaires pertinentes tout en consolidant la localisation et en renforçant le leadership des organisations féminines, le Coordonnateur Humanitaire, après consultation du Comité Consultatif du FH RCA, lance une allocation de $8 millions (dont un minimum de 45% directement pour les ONG Nationales incluant les WLO), visant à :     Maintenir une capacité opérationnelle dans les zones prioritaires où les partenaires restent disponibles et pertinents ;     Financer directement des réponses menées par des WLO, notamment dans les zones où l’accès est limité ;     Renforcer les capacités institutionnelles et techniques des WLO, y compris via des projets portés par d’autres acteurs ;     Prioriser les zones ayant généré le plus grand nombre d’alertes humanitaires et touchant le plus grand nombre de personnes au cours des 12 derniers mois ;     Préserver une capacité de réponse rapide, permettant de traiter les besoins déjà identifiés ainsi que les nouvelles alertes.          Cette approche permettra de maintenir la présence humanitaire, de renforcer le leadership des WLO et d’assurer une allocation flexible et réactive, tout en contribuant à l’agenda de localisation et à la protection des populations.

Colombia atraviesa una crisis humanitaria agravada en 2025 por el conflicto armado interno, desastres naturales y el aumento de la movilidad humana, especialmente de migrantes y refugiados, en medio de la expansión de Grupos Armados No Estatales que ejercen control violento sobre territorios y población civil; ante la disminución de fondos humanitarios, se prioriza fortalecer la respuesta local y avanzar hacia soluciones sostenibles, por lo que el Fondo Humanitario Regional para América Latina y el Caribe ha asignado 1.5 millones de dólares para apoyar intervenciones en zonas vulnerables, enfocadas en mecanismos de respuesta rápida y protección comunitaria, con énfasis en Guaviare, Vichada, Caquetá, Valle del Cauca y Magdalena Medio.

This allocation will support a six-month multisectoral response, including food security, health, water, sanitation and hygiene (WASH), protection, shelter, and nutrition. Where feasible, cash-based assistance will be prioritized to enhance flexibility, dignity, and efficiency. The allocation will also include critical enablers to support operations in hard-to-reach areas.
